newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges softer, cargoes talked strong.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges softer, cargoes talked strong.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges traded a little weaker early on Tuesday with traders saying low demand sapped the market, while Russian cargoes were still offered at strong numbers due to scarcity.
High sulphur fuel barges traded at $86.25 a tonne fob three times in Rotterdam and Antwerp compared with Monday's closing level of $87.25/$87.50 and initial deals at $86.25/$86.75.
Later talk was at $86/$87, traders said.
"Buyers are now around $86. It was mainly due to crude's fall (yesterday) and also there is not too many bunker enquiries," one Rotterdam-based trader said of the move.
Bunker suppliers said demand looked set to be no higher than 10,000 tonnes, the same as a day earlier.
A trader with a major said the barge market would be steady to weak this week but may rise next week "as many people have limitations on their contract deliveries."
Low sulphur barges were steady in a quietly-talked market with buyers at $94 and sellers at $2 higher, after a trade on Monday at $95.
"These levels are notional. That's what's wrong with this market, you can not really test the sellers because there's no demand really," one trader said.

High sulphur Russian cracked cargoes were talked at two means plus $2, traders said, while M-100 straight-run was talked as high as two means plus $6, which would put it around the 90 cif mark, while E-4 was offered some $1 higher at three means plus $5.
